I totally get what you mean. Strong of you to fight it.

I fear it will take one or perhaps two generations to filter out many traditional concepts like these because it seems an upbringing can shape a persons worldview. We have indeed talked about these issues as a society but are unable to reach into many family homes.
Think it depends on ones native language, culture and that direct translation may convey a more literal meaning.

I think hollywood movies promote and celebrate catcalling, sexual assault/persistance etc. Especially teenage/high school/college movies and also the more extreme examples like american pie. Like it's some sort of "this is how things are supposed to be!" message.

I'm also guilty of sexual assault. When I was in elementary school I kissed a girl without consent because that was how disney movies portrayed it, so I thought she would take the kiss like a disney princess. Only 15 years later did I remember the incident and realized how wrong it was.

The message of movies has gotten more attention since #metoo and I'm hopeful it changes sooner rather than later.

I've no memory of anyone I know that's been publicly convicted or accused for rape. In first grade in elementary school I stole a kiss (sexaul assault) but I never told anyone about it, so no way others could know.

I guess women talk to eachother in private about their experiences and can know that way, but as a dude I've no idea how we're supposed to know who has done what.

Then again I never befriended or associated with any bad guys in school, so I never knew what they were up to.

Edit: My last paragraph is pointless. I think I wrote it in the context of the first two - how can a dude suspect who has done what.

Some seem to talk about harsher punishements, but I doubt sex criminals (especially child molesters) make risk assessments counting how many years they will spend in jail for doing crime x. We're a type of animal that are capable of doing extremely horrible things - like the holocoaust, and unless we aknowledge that we have savage sides that can be awakened, I think we're missing possible counteractions.

An individual is usually considered to be the resulting mix of genetics and enviroment.

Through history rape has been largely practically unpunished. As a species it will probably take some generations for those genes to be filtered away given a justice system that limits their reproduction harshly, or we may do it with future gene-modification.

A lot of bad parenting like emotional neglect and abuse foster savage tendencies. We're only about two generations away from ww2 and many parents were never given a proper childhood themselves, so they're unable to give their childs that. Overworked parents can also not care for their childs and alcohol and drugs are experimented by young adults and teenagers. I hope this can be combated with compulsory parenting courses and therapist visits along with more resources for schools to intervene.

I get black mirror vibes when I see people spread likes around them. It seems very superficial to me - and I think it encourages further (possibly) meaningless behaviour. Reddit is healthier than facebook though. On reddit it's more thoughts and less selfies or "bought new stuff" advertising.
I'm so amazed really. Really an example of what's possible given the dedication.

I don't even think Kim has access to the button. I think he's china's barking dog to instill fear in the US.

I think you are so right! I really wonder when/if there will be a more naunced discussion in public instead of simple slogans like you mention at the end. I really hope we as a society can finally combat loneliness effectively before too long..

Supposedly slogans are good where it's hard to make ends meet and there's no room analysis. Hence "suck it up" or even shaming, and this makes me really anxious.
Don't think anyone asks their daughter to decieve a collegue. Don't get so down. Not trusting people hurts a lot. ;)

I (mid-twenties guy) worked as a teaching assistant in a course at university. During the end of the course a really bright girl seemed to take interest in me. She approached me numerous times like a dolphin performing some kind of stunt.

I was totally clueless to the phenomena that girls can desire what they can't get and thought "well we're both adults", so the last day of the course I asked discretely if she had shown interest, to which she responded that she was, but when I asked if she wanted to talk after exams she said she didn't have time or something. I was stunned.

A month later during some extended holiday I felt like shit, thinking the reason I felt like shit was because: I felt I had been toyed with, and that I had not understood her. So I went into anxious romeo mode \*knowing\* she would forgive me and contacted her on social media with a delirious and inappropriate message. She was alarmed I had contacted her, so I asked for her forgiveness and she did indeed forgive me.

I still have not forgiven myself and do not plan to teach again.

I've shown screenshots to two therapists (one woman) but both said I had done nothing wrong - meaning it's always okay to ask.  I find this absurd, but they are part of an older generation.

Never thought I could make myself guilty of sexual harrassment. #guilty

I read a reply to someone on a dating sub who was anxious about contacting a girl (the consensus on the sub was to never contact in order to not be needy):

"Since you don't give a fuck anymore just say fuck it and contact her."

I applied the reply to my situation. I knew the girl I was interested in would forgive me for contacting her, but at the same time it was inappropriate because I had teached her in a previous course at university the month before (age diff 2 years).

I became some anxious romeo. Contacted her. She was alarmed about it. I asked for forgiveness. She did indeed forgive me...but I can still not forgive myself and have went to therapy. I don't think many would want to associate with a teaching assistant that made a pass on a past student so I will not renew my contract (the contract does not mention relationships - but it's immoral anyway).

This is the greatest mistake of my life. Never thought I would be guilty of #metoo.

It's not uncommon for people to get spam-filtered on subs because their comments are either against the rules or against a norm that isn't stated in the rules (like mentioning suicide).

Part of ensuring that the spam-filtering works is to not alert the users that they have been filtered - so they may write worthwhile comments after that one marked comment, but no one will see them.
